what_it_does: The sustainment/logistics C2 layer converts transactional logistics records (requisitions, maintenance work orders, ammunition/fuel stock levels, personnel/medical status, cargo movements) into a time-relevant common operating picture and decision support for commanders and sustainers, and pushes resulting tasks back out (resupply missions, movement orders, maintenance priorities). It sits between enterprise ERPs and transportation systems (GCSS-Army, LMP, GCSS-MC, Navy ERP/NOSS, DLA EBS, USTRANSCOM IGC/GDSS) and operational C2/COP tools (CPCE, NGC2, Onebrief plans, JADC2 data fabrics). Core functions: data collection from ERPs, sensors and RFID/ITV feeds; fusion into logistics status and running estimates (days of supply, consumption forecasts, readiness rates); distribution and movement planning; predictive maintenance; and dissemination of sustainment orders. Its distinctive difficulty is that the source systems are centralized, connectivity-dependent business systems while the consumers operate at the tactical edge under DDIL conditions.

current_architecture.description: Service-siloed transactional ERPs feed enterprise data lakes and dashboards (Army Vantage/ADP, Advana/Pegasus, BLADE), while the tactical sustainment picture is assembled largely by staff from LOGSTAT reports, spreadsheets, email and voice, then re-entered into C2 tools (CPCE) or briefing slides. Transportation C2 is separate (IGC for ITV, GDSS for air mobility, TC-AIMS II for unit movement). Joint plans (JOPES/JPES TPFDD) are loosely coupled to actual stock and movement data. The Army's attempt to consolidate the ERPs (EBS-C) was effectively paused in May 2026 when the Army declined the second-year option, leaving the integration problem open and shifting emphasis to modernizing existing systems.

current_architecture.security_domain: Predominantly NIPR/CUI (IL4-IL5) for ERPs and readiness dashboards; SIPR for OPLAN-linked sustainment feasibility, theater and joint COPs, TPFDD and JLOC operations; some analytics mirrored to SIPR/JWICS (Advana - RECALL). Coalition sharing is ad hoc.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: High. ERPs are centralized and require reach-back; GCSS-Army disconnected operations are limited to tablet-based store-and-forward (RECALL). Enterprise dashboards (Vantage, Advana) are unusable without connectivity. Tactical reporting falls back to FM voice, email, JBC-P free text and spreadsheets.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: LOGSTATs revert to voice and Excel; requisitions queue and later collide; ITV goes dark between nodes; commanders lose days-of-supply and readiness visibility; on reconnect, duplicate or conflicting entries must be reconciled by hand; plan assumptions drift from reality for hours to days.

technical_difficulty.summary: Moderate core software difficulty, high integration difficulty. The algorithms (days-of-supply math, consumption factors, routing, forecasting) are well understood; the hard parts are (1) offline-first data synchronization and conflict resolution across intermittently connected nodes, (2) canonical data modeling across SAP/Oracle ERPs, DLMS transactions, RFID/ITV feeds and free-text LOGSTATs, (3) producing trustworthy fused status when sources disagree or are stale, and (4) meeting ATO/IL5 and eventually SIPR requirements while keeping a modern UX.
required_expertise: Offline-first distributed systems (CRDTs, store-and-forward, delta sync over low-bandwidth links)
Enterprise integration with SAP/Oracle and DLMS/EDI transaction standards
Data engineering and schema mapping / entity resolution
Sustainment doctrine (FM 4-0, ATP 4-90, OPLOG planning factors, LOGSTAT reporting)
DoD security engineering (NIST 800-171/CMMC, RMF ATO, IL4/IL5 hosting)
Frontend/HMI for staff workflows under stress
Light ML for demand forecasting and anomaly detection
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Bidirectional, trustworthy synchronization between the connectivity-dependent enterprise ERPs and edge nodes that must keep operating (and issuing requests) while disconnected, then reconciling without creating duplicate requisitions or corrupting the enterprise system of record.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Dashboards, mapping, generic forecasting models, cloud hosting, mesh/satellite transport hardware (from others), RFID readers, LLM summarization of reports.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: two founders, synthetic data conforming to public doctrine formats (LOGSTAT, OPLOG planning factors) and simulated GCSS-Army exports; no ATO. Credible demo: SBIR Phase I/II or OTA-funded, participation in a warfighter exercise or NGC2/Project Convergence-style event, CUI-capable environment, a GovCloud IL4/IL5 sandbox, one integration (e.g., GCSS-Army extract or CPCE/NGC2 API), 4-8 staff for 12-18 months. Production: ATO/IL5, CMMC Level 2, integration with AESIP/GCSS-Army via the program office, sustainment/helpdesk, possibly SIPR instance, 15-30 staff over 2-3 years. Government-funded R&D can offset a large share; the $250k founder capital covers PoC only.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - doctrine, forms, planning factors and exercise scenarios are public and allow a convincing synthetic PoC, but real GCSS-Army/LIW/IGC data is CUI and requires a government sponsor and data-use agreement.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Yes for credibility beyond PoC: GCSS-Army/LMP extracts, LIW readiness data, ITV feeds, unit LOGSTATs; typically arranged through a sponsoring unit, CFT or program office under CUI handling rules.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Generic logistics software is usually not ITAR-controlled, but maintenance/technical data about specific weapon systems and some military-critical logistics information can be export-controlled (ITAR or EAR/CUI export-controlled category). Needs specialist review before any non-US person touches the data or code paths handling it.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - nearly all real inputs are CUI (readiness, stock levels, unit locations); NIST SP 800-171/CMMC Level 2 will be required in contracts.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - theater/joint sustainment tied to OPLANs, TPFDD and JLOC operate on SIPR; a tactical-echelon product can stay unclassified longer than a joint planning product.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not required for an unclassified MVP; at least one cleared (Secret) engineer/founder becomes necessary for exercise integration and SIPR deployment; facility clearance needed for classified contracts.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: Constraints to review with counsel, not legal conclusions: (1) SBIR/STTR eligibility requires the company to be more than 50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents - an Indonesian founder who is not a US person counts against this, so cap-table structure matters (the German founder's permanent residency would count once granted); (2) CUI handling and export-controlled technical data may restrict a non-US person's access to data and certain code, requiring a technology control plan; (3) security clearances require US citizenship, so the non-US founder cannot hold one; (4) significant foreign ownership/control can trigger FOCI mitigation requirements for cleared work; (5) many DoD program offices informally prefer all-US-person teams for logistics data access. A structure where the non-US-person founder leads commercial/product and stays segregated from CUI/export-controlled data is common but needs specialist legal review.

why_not_solved.explanation: Sustainment data lives in SAP and Oracle ERPs with decades of customization, DLMS transaction routing and service-specific schemas; every C2 integration is a bespoke, program-office-mediated project. The 2026 EBS-C retreat shows even the Army with a $1B-ceiling SI could not push consolidation through.

The ERP owner (PEO EIS/PEO MLB), the C2 owner (PEO C3T), the data owner (AMC/LDAC), the requirements owner (CL CFT/CASCOM/G-4) and the joint movement owner (USTRANSCOM) are different organizations with different budgets; no single buyer owns the plan-to-reality bridge.

Palantir Vantage/ADP and Advana are the sanctioned enterprise data layers; new entrants are expected to plug into them, and the Palantir EA makes extending the incumbent the path of least resistance for the Army.

Offline-first sync (CRDTs), cheap mesh/satellite links (Starlink-class), and modern open C2 data layers (NGC2) only matured 2022-2026, making a tactical sustainment product that survives DDIL practical now.

Tactical sustainment software is a small dollar market compared with fires/ISR C2; large integrators prioritize O&M task orders; VCs favored ISR, autonomy and fires. Result: few well-capitalized entrants (Rune is a rare exception).
Real readiness/stock data is CUI and controlled by AMC/LDAC, DLA and program offices; startups cannot train or validate without a sponsor, slowing iteration.
Plan-coupled sustainment (OPLAN feasibility, TPFDD) lives on SIPR, pushing the highest-value use cases behind clearance and facility barriers.

Predictive logistics/maintenance has cycled through SBIR and pilots (Uptake, SBIR performers) without a scaled tactical product; enterprise dashboards exist but the edge-to-enterprise loop remains manual - not for lack of trying but for lack of an owner and a survivable architecture.

attractiveness.bull: Real, documented, repeatedly acknowledged pain (2018 COP article, 2025 swivel-chair, 2026 ITV CSO, GAO Indo-Pacific reports); an unprecedented number of open procurement doors for software (Palantir EA, Onebrief and Govini enterprise IDIQs prove the Army will put commercial software on enterprise vehicles); NGC2 explicitly opens an integration layer where sustainment data has to land; the EBS-C collapse leaves an integration void that will be filled by middleware, not a new ERP; Rune's funding shows investors will back tactical logistics software; the core algorithms are unglamorous but tractable for a strong engineer; a small team can produce a credible exercise-ready prototype on SBIR money.
attractiveness.bear: Palantir (Vantage/ADP, EA) and Anduril/Lockheed (NGC2) sit exactly where a bridge product would live and can absorb the feature; Rune Technologies has a multi-year head start with ex-Marine founders; all valuable data is CUI and sponsor-gated; a non-US-person co-founder complicates SBIR eligibility and data access; the buyer is fragmented and slow; predictive-logistics sub-segment shows proto-purgatory; the total addressable market at tactical echelon is modest, so the realistic exit is acquisition by an integrator, not a standalone company; competing with SI incumbents on ERP integration is not viable for two students.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium attractiveness: a legitimate wedge exists at the enterprise-to-tactical sustainment status bridge and at plan-coupled consumption forecasting, but it is a narrow, integrator-dependent, sponsor-gated market where the founders' immigration profile and lack of operational credibility are real handicaps; pursue only with a uniformed sustainment co-founder/advisor and an NGC2/CL CFT sponsor.

market_stage.rationale: Enterprise analytics/planning software has crossed into production vehicles (Palantir EA, Govini and Onebrief IDIQs) while the tactical/ITV edge is still at the solicitation-and-prototype stage (TRANSCOM CSO May 2026, NGC2 prototypes) and the ERP consolidation attempt regressed in 2026. Mixed signals across sub-segments indicate a transitioning market: mature at enterprise data layer, prototyping at the edge, stagnant in predictive logistics point solutions.

proto_purgatory.notes: Predictive logistics/maintenance shows classic purgatory: Uptake Army pilots (~2019, RECALL), C3 AI PANDA enterprise contract with uneven fleet adoption (RECALL), multiple SBIR Phase I/II awards (Forward Edge-AI, Modus Operandi, PacMar, Navy blockchain logistics, USSF ASCN) without verified production transitions. Contested logistics CFT has produced demonstrations but no software program of record found. Counter-signal: planning/data platforms (Onebrief, Govini, Palantir) did escape purgatory via enterprise IDIQs and an EA in 2025-2026.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for standalone predictive-analytics or blockchain point solutions; opportunity for workflow products that ride an existing enterprise vehicle (NGC2 ecosystem, Onebrief/Govini partner integrations, Palantir EA) and solve a staff workflow rather than promising AI insight.

candidate_gaps.title: Edge-to-enterprise sustainment status bridge (LOGSTAT-to-COP automation under DDIL)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Battalion-to-division sustainment status (Class I/III/V, maintenance, medical) is still hand-assembled from GCSS-Army extracts, voice reports and spreadsheets and re-entered into C2 tools, so the commander's sustainment picture lags hours to a day and collapses when disconnected.
candidate_gaps.user: Battalion S4, BSB SPO, division G4/DSB staff; NGC2 users at 4th ID/25th ID; USMC CLE staff
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Company XO/1SG estimates or pulls GCSS-Army status when connected; 2) S4 fills LOGSTAT spreadsheet/DA form; 3) sends via email, JBC-P free text or FM voice; 4) BSB SPO consolidates by hand and computes days of supply; 5) G4 re-enters into CPCE, a sync matrix or PowerPoint; 6) commander briefs from slides; 7) on reconnect, requisitions submitted offline are re-keyed into GCSS-Army.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: CPCE sustainment widgets / Logistics Reporting Tool (RECALL), Vantage dashboards (enterprise, connectivity-dependent), CLC2S (USMC, web app), Rune TyrOS (early stage), and manual staff work.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No offline-first, doctrinally structured sustainment ledger that syncs to both the ERP and the C2 data layer; duplicates and stale data on reconnect; no bidirectional link between plan and stock reality.

candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: An offline-first sustainment ledger (CRDT-based, delta-sync over any link) with a doctrinal LOGSTAT/OPLOG schema, auto-computed running estimates, and thin adapters into GCSS-Army exports, CoT/NGC2 APIs and Onebrief plans - positioned as the neutral 'sustainment data transport' rather than another dashboard.

candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Public doctrine planning factors (FM 4-0, ATP 4-90, OPLOG Planner factors); GCSS-Army report formats (CUI, via sponsor); unit LOGSTAT templates; later LIW/Vantage APIs.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: GCSS-Army/AESIP extracts, CPCE and NGC2 data layer APIs, JBC-P/CoT, Onebrief plan objects; ATO IL4/IL5; CMMC L2.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army SBIR (Contested Logistics topic), xTech, CL CFT sponsorship, NGC2 vendor ecosystem, DIU CSO, Onebrief/Govini partner integration; later Palantir EA co-selling or an ACC IDIQ.
candidate_gaps.why_now: NGC2 open integration layer (2025-2026), CL CFT priorities, EBS-C retreat, mesh/satellite connectivity at edge, and Army willingness to put commercial software on enterprise IDIQs (Onebrief Sept 2026).
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Army decides sustainment data flows only through Palantir/NGC2 integrators, leaving no room for an independent bridge; or Rune closes the gap first.

candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: USTRANSCOM lacks near real-time, end-to-end ITV that fuses RFID, satellite trackers, carrier EDI and manifests into a trusted COP that survives contested and disconnected legs.
candidate_gaps.user: USTRANSCOM DDOC/Fusion Center, 618th AOC, theater distribution centers, TSC distribution management
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Cargo tagged (RFID/barcode) and manifested in service systems (TC-AIMS II etc.); 2) reads flow into IGC ITV server with gaps between nodes; 3) staff query IGC, carrier portals and email; 4) Pegasus/Advana analytics on aggregated, delayed data; 5) manual phone/email chasing for high-priority items.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: IGC ITV, GDSS, carrier EDI, Pegasus on Advana; Turbo Fusion trialed NADACS/mesh.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Latency and gaps between tracking sources; no fusion of heterogeneous feeds; dependence on fixed RFID infrastructure; not designed for contested legs.

candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Ingest synthetic/open feeds (AIS, ADS-B, simulated RFID reads, EDI 214/315 status messages), produce fused shipment tracks with confidence, degrade gracefully when feeds drop; demo against a Turbo Fusion-like scenario.

candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Operational plans built in tools like Onebrief are not automatically checked against fuel, ammunition and parts reality, so sustainment feasibility is a manual staff estimate that goes stale as the plan changes.
candidate_gaps.user: Division/corps G4 planners, TSC/ESC planners, CCMD J4 and JLOC, USTRANSCOM planners
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Planners draft courses of action in Onebrief/PowerPoint; 2) G4 runs OPLOG Planner-style factors in spreadsheets; 3) stock and readiness data pulled from GCSS-Army/Vantage/LIW; 4) sustainment estimate briefed as a static slide; 5) plan changes require re-running by hand; 6) at joint level, TPFDD feasibility analyzed separately.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Manual OPLOG-style estimation, Vantage dashboards, Govini Ark (enterprise supply chain), Onebrief (planning without deep logistics estimation - INFERENCE).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No live link between plan objects (units, tasks, distances, tempo) and consumption/stock models; classification boundary for OPLANs.
